## Follow the operation, not a reference count

The source-direction question remains $B_n \to R_n \to B_{n+1} \to R_{n+1}$, with $R=(G,M)$. This reading map connects particular operations to sources under stated conditions. It supplements the [current catalogue](/evidence/catalogue/); it does not add cases to that scientific document or promote the predecessor edition back to current authority.

The H connections below are **proposed editorial links to parts of the claims in 08_claim_coverage.md v0.2.1**, not endorsements of each entire compound statement. Result type and relevance are independent labels. A paper, a publication version, a dataset, and a project case interpretation are different units. Multiple URLs are not independent confirmations, and one DOI does not guarantee independent study/data. Linked manuscripts can differ from the publication; findings are not merged merely because their lineage matches.

## Document and edition qualified labels

Use the source document, its edition and its local label together. In particular, **04 C1 means possibility-space growth; 06 C1 means geometry–mode reciprocity**. H labels refer to 08 claim coverage. The two E01 labels below refer to different papers. Current 06 E07 and predecessor 08 E08 share BIB-0036 and represent one study.

## Current case connections

Read depth below is dated and scoped; original audit inspection is not relabelled as a new website paper audit. Use each linked case for its full source-reported finding, conditions and inspection details.

### 06 E01 — Experimental Study of the Triplet Synchronization of Coupled Nonidentical Mechanical Metronomes

[E01 reading](/claims/UT-E101/) · :cite[BIB-0066]

**Result type:** experiment. **Relevance:** component / constraint. **Partial-claim connections:** H04.

Coupled nonidentical metronomes exhibit a collective triplet synchronization relation even where individual pairs are asynchronous.

**Supplied:** Metronomes, their energy supply, and mechanical coupling already exist. **Limit:** Collective coordination need not mean every oscillator has one identical frequency or phase. This does not demonstrate the creation of the oscillators.

**Locator:** 06_evidence_catalog.md E01; original-paper location as reported there **Read depth:** Source-reported 2026-10-02: Publisher HTML, including experimental description. Not a fresh website paper audit.

### 06 E02 — Controlling the motion of multiple objects on a Chladni plate

[E02 reading](/claims/UT-E102/) · :cite[BIB-0067]

**Result type:** experiment. **Relevance:** component. **Partial-claim connections:** H05, H20.

Plate vibrations can transport particles; the study uses controlled sequences of excitation to manipulate multiple objects.

**Supplied:** A manufactured plate, particles, actuator, camera and control algorithm are provided. **Limit:** Distinguish ordinary nodal accumulation from the paper’s actively controlled manipulation. Neither establishes autonomous particle-to-field feedback or reproduction.

**Locator:** 06_evidence_catalog.md E02; original-paper location as reported there **Read depth:** Source-reported 2026-10-02: Publisher HTML and author-institution abstract. Supplementary videos linked on the paper page were not watched. Not a fresh website paper audit.

### 06 E03 — Independent trapping and manipulation of microparticles using dexterous acoustic tweezers

[E03 reading](/claims/UT-E103/) · :cite[BIB-0068]

**Result type:** experiment. **Relevance:** component. **Partial-claim connections:** H05, H20.

A phased ultrasonic array independently traps and manipulates microparticles; reported examples include 45 and 90 micrometre spheres.

**Supplied:** An engineered transducer array, liquid medium and pre-existing particles are required. **Limit:** This particular experiment supports microscale manipulation, not a claim of nanoscale performance or a universal size–frequency law.

**Locator:** 06_evidence_catalog.md E03; original-paper location as reported there **Read depth:** Source-reported 2026-10-02: Author-institution records and original-paper abstract; not a full methods or data audit. Not a fresh website paper audit.

### 06 E04 — Noise-induced spatial periodicity in excitable chemical media

[E04 reading](/claims/UT-E104/) · :cite[BIB-0069]

**Result type:** simulation. **Relevance:** component. **Partial-claim connections:** H01, H02.

Numerical excitable-chemical-media dynamics show an intermediate noise regime with enhanced spatial periodicity.

**Supplied:** An Oregonator-type reaction model, diffusion, parameter choices and noisy forcing are specified. **Limit:** This is a numerical result, not a laboratory observation of the primordial background. Noise acts through existing nonlinear dynamics.

**Locator:** 06_evidence_catalog.md E04; original-paper location as reported there **Read depth:** Source-reported 2026-10-02: Primary publisher record and abstract; equations and simulation data not independently reproduced. Not a fresh website paper audit.

### 06 E05 — Transition from a uniform state to hexagonal and striped Turing patterns

[E05 reading](/claims/UT-E105/) · :cite[BIB-0070]

**Result type:** experiment. **Relevance:** component / comparator. **Partial-claim connections:** H02.

A chemically supplied reaction–diffusion experiment produces stationary patterned states from a uniform regime.

**Supplied:** Specific reactions, diffusion, gel geometry and reagent supply are provided. **Limit:** A stationary spatial mode is not automatically a temporal oscillation or a self-maintaining resonator. Uniform-state instability is not identical to noise-induced ordering.

**Locator:** 06_evidence_catalog.md E05; original-paper location as reported there **Read depth:** Source-reported 2026-10-02: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record. Not a fresh website paper audit.

### 06 E06 — Resonant pattern formation in a chemical system

[E06 reading](/claims/UT-E106/) · :cite[BIB-0071]

**Result type:** experiment. **Relevance:** partial bridge. **Partial-claim connections:** H05, H04.

Periodic illumination of a photosensitive chemical oscillator locks responses to the forcing and changes the spatial pattern. External temporal forcing changes spatial patterns; H04 is context only, not measured mutual oscillator coupling.

**Supplied:** The reaction medium and periodic optical drive are supplied externally. **Limit:** The experiment links temporal forcing and spatial organization, not the spontaneous origin of the drive or new fundamental laws.

**Locator:** 06_evidence_catalog.md E06; original-paper location as reported there **Read depth:** Source-reported 2026-10-02: Publisher abstract and record. Not a fresh website paper audit.

### 06 E07 — Dicke quantum phase transition with a superfluid gas in an optical cavity

[E07 reading](/claims/UT-E107/) · :cite[BIB-0036]

**Result type:** experiment. **Relevance:** partial bridge. **Partial-claim connections:** H03, H06.

A pumped atom–cavity system undergoes a collective transition with mutually coupled matter organization and optical-field dynamics.

**Supplied:** Atoms, cavity boundaries and laser pumping are given. **Limit:** This is a close geometry–field feedback example, but not unstructured matter producing its own complete apparatus or successive autonomous levels.

**Locator:** Primary paper abstract: Dicke transition and atom–cavity self-organization; 06 E07. **Read depth:** Source-reported 2026-10-02: Publisher abstract and article record. Not a fresh website paper audit.

### 06 E08 — Tunable colloidal swarmalators with hydrodynamic coupling

[E08 reading](/claims/UT-E108/) · :cite[BIB-0002]

**Result type:** experiment. **Relevance:** partial bridge. **Partial-claim connections:** H03, H04.

## Environmental feedback and effective interactions

Ratzke and Gore's **experiment and qualitative model** shows bacterial pH changes feeding back on growth, including facilitation, inhibition and harmful outcomes in supplied cultures (:cite[BIB-0089], Results and Figures 1–4). This is supplementary component/feedback context for 08 H06/H09/H13/H17; it does not demonstrate a new species or a universal resonant mechanism. Primary HTML result and caption text was inspected on 5 October 2026; data were not reproduced.

The original Bardeen–Cooper–Schrieffer **theory** provides a conditional phonon-mediated-attraction anchor (:cite[BIB-0090], abstract). It is effective-interaction context for 08 H15, not an experimental replication. Only the primary abstract and identity were inspected on 5 October 2026. Keep :cite[BIB-0016] as specialist context.

Spin ice provides distinct theoretical quasiparticle context (:cite[BIB-0017]), bulk-material measurement (:cite[BIB-0018]) and artificial-kagome observation (:cite[BIB-0019]). These platforms and their evidence types remain separate; they do not derive all fundamental interactions. CERN's background-state explanations (:cite[BIB-0020], :cite[BIB-0021]) concern spectra and interaction regimes, rather than the identical mechanism as material-mediated attraction.

## Methods, background and optional applications

Mori (:cite[BIB-0077]), controlled amplitude approximation (:cite[BIB-0084]), Kron reduction (:cite[BIB-0049]) and coarse-grained Langevin memory (:cite[BIB-0051]) help construct reduced descriptions. They are method context, not physical creation of a new medium. Coupled-resonator theory (:cite[BIB-0007]) supplies both a method and constraints on specified open-resonator approximations. AI/learning sources (:cite[BIB-0001], :cite[BIB-0056], :cite[BIB-0057]) remain related work; no RRG benchmark gain follows from them.

Nuclear-network/Chemical Organization Theory (:cite[BIB-0044], :cite[BIB-0045]) belongs to one publication lineage: ALIFE 2025 and a later January 2026 arXiv version. The [author-institution publication record](https://researchportal.vub.be/en/publications/emergent-complexity-in-nuclear-reaction-networks-a-study-of-stell/) identifies DOI 10.1162/ISAL.a.914. Metadata relation was checked on 5 October 2026; equivalence of the complete texts was not established.

The catalogue's F01 is orientation, F02 is optional effective-Hamiltonian theory, and F03 is optional mathematics. F03's listed issue date is 25 October 2026; its first-online date remains unestablished here. Versions, supplementary videos, data and code are access paths or children of publications, not automatically independent confirmations. No media or datasets were reproduced for this map.
